animalsNote: EVERY VISIBLE ANIMAL AT ITS TRUE SIZE (errata 201 for the horses; errata 205 for the rest). Each entry is measured by tests/scale.test.ts as the engine draws it, against the room's man where the animal stands: `top` (read from the sheet's top opaque row in `columns`, or `topRow`) and its feet (the bottom opaque row, or `feetRow`, or a room y in `feetY` when they are hidden). `groundY` names the floor the man is taken at when the animal is not standing on the room's floor at its anchor (a crate, a hole in a rise). Above the walk band the man is the curve carried on in a straight line, which is what a flat floor's perspective does. `basis` says where each range comes from. An entry with `knownWrong` is a measured failure recorded for Tyler and printed on every run: the test fails if it is fixed and the entry is left in.

figuresNote: EVERY FIGURE BESIDE THAD, AS DRAWN (errata 234; Tyler, 2026-11-09: "the screenshot you sent shows Thad looking much smaller than everyone else. It all needs to be scaled correctly. Similarly through the whole game."). tests/scale-vs-thad.test.mjs measures every visible figure's crown-to-sole IN SCREEN PIXELS, through the engine's own scale, against Thad's at the same soles (tools/audit-scale-vs-thad.mjs). A standing adult is held to 0.97-1.03 of Thad (errata 235; 0.95-1.05 under errata 234). An entry here says how to read a figure the pixels cannot: `eyeRow` and `chinRow` (a hatted head: its crown is 0.9 of the eyes-to-chin above the eyes, the share measured on the hatless cast), `crownRow` and `soleRow` (declared rows), `columns` (a group's tallest adult, which also needs `held`), `groundY` (the floor a man is held to when he is not standing on it: a man up a ladder). `expect` replaces 0.97-1.03 and must cite a ruling (`ruling`, `by`). `knownWrong` is a measured failure recorded for Tyler: printed on every run, and the test fails when it is fixed and the entry is left in. `room` limits an entry to one placement.
